info.name: racket
info.category: Compiled to bytecode on the Chez Scheme VM (Racket CS)
info.typing: Dynamically typed; optional contracts (define/contract) and Typed Racket
info.gc: Yes — generational (inherited from the Chez Scheme runtime)
info.runtime: Racket CS — the Chez Scheme VM (since Racket 8)
info.design_notes: Racket is a Scheme descendant built for language-oriented programming. Since version 8 it compiles to Chez Scheme bytecode (Racket CS) with a generational collector. Its `define/contract` forms add runtime boundary checks (kept here, as that is the LeetCode Racket shape), and immutable pairs plus dynamic dispatch mean arithmetic-heavy code trails the native and JVM languages; its strength is expressiveness and macros.
key_traits: S-expression homoiconicity and a powerful macro system
Contracts add runtime checks at function boundaries
Generational GC; singly-linked lists favor cons/recur over indexing
Chez-backed JIT-style compilation; startup boots the VM + modules
info.peak_speed: Several× to ~15× slower than C++ on arithmetic
